You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

An economist undertakes a cost-benefit analysis of the pollution resulting from a manufacturing process. Which judgement is most likely to guide any recommendation about the appropriate level of manufacturing output?

options.A: that the marginal social cost of manufacturing equals the marginal social benefit
options.B: that the marginal cost of pollution is zero
options.C: that the total revenue of manufacturing equals the total cost
options.D: that the total benefit of pollution is maximised

questions.questionText: An individual consumes goods X and Y. The marginal utility of good X is positive and falling. The consumer is at the point where the ratio of the marginal utility of the two goods is equal to the ratio of their prices. What can be concluded from this information?

options.A: the consumer will continue to consume additional units of X until marginal utility is zero
options.B: the consumer will purchase more of X if the price of Y rises
options.C: total utility will be negative on the additional unit of X consumed
options.D: total utility will be rising at an increasing rate on the additional unit of X consumed

questions.questionText: To analyse a consumer’s preferences, an indifference curve represents possible combinations of goods X and Y. The diagram shows a consumer’s indifference curve for good X and good Y. units of I good Y E F G I O units of good X What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Point E is the most desirable combination.
options.B: Point F is less desirable than point G.
options.C: Point G is the least desirable combination.
options.D: Points E, F and G are equally desirable combinations.

questions.questionText: Labour from developing countries often migrates to developed countries and finds jobs. How would such a movement of labour be likely to affect the economic growth and the pressure on wage rises in the developed country? economic growth pressure on wage rises
The African Union consists of 55 developing countries. They agree to adopt a free-trade model to boost trade between member countries. In theory what do free-trade models tend to ignore?

options.A: absolute advantage in terms of lower factor inputs in production
options.B: allocation of resources where comparative cost advantage is greatest
options.C: the international division of labour and differences in opportunity cost ratios
options.D: transport costs and inefficiencies in the handling of goods and services

questions.questionText: Young workers find it especially difficult to get a job during an economic recession. A government introduces a transfer payment for those seeking work and provides information on vacancies. What should be a positive outcome of this policy for those seeking work?

options.A: Firms no longer need to advertise jobs because there are few vacancies.
options.B: No production of goods or services is required for a transfer payment.
options.C: Obtaining information on jobs available makes the labour market more perfect.
options.D: Students will leave their studies to join the workforce at an earlier age.

What belief do Keynesians and Monetarists share?

options.A: Expectations rapidly adapt to changing circumstances.
options.B: Fiscal policy is the most effective economic policy.
options.C: There is need for individual choice expressed through the market.
options.D: The velocity of circulation of money is stable.

questions.questionText: Which statement is most likely to be made by an economist from the Keynesian school?

options.A: Any deviation from full employment will only be temporary.
options.B: Free markets will always lead to an efficient economic outcome.
options.C: Market imperfections can lead the economy to remain below full capacity for a considerable time.
options.D: The role of expansionary fiscal policy is likely to be limited.

questions.questionText: The US government has been using a policy of quantitative easing to increase economic growth. What is the most likely effect of this policy on the internal and external value of the US dollar? internal value external value
In 2018 the US imposed a tariff on steel imports. What is the likely impact of this tariff on the US economy?

options.A: It will make US steel exports more price competitive.
options.B: It will lead to productive inefficiency in the US steel industry.
options.C: There will be a deterioration in the US’s terms of trade.
